summary: This program models a printer's waiting list using a Queue backed by a LinkedList. Four filenames are added to the back of the queue, then a loop repeatedly reports how many jobs are left, looks at the next one, and removes it until the queue is empty.

lines.text: Queue is the interface that describes first-in, first-out behaviour: items leave in the same order they arrived, which is exactly how a printer should work.
LinkedList is the concrete class that supplies the actual storage; Queue on its own cannot be created with new.
Declaring the variable as Queue but building a LinkedList means the rest of the code can only use queue operations, which keeps the FIFO discipline honest.
offer adds an element to the tail of the queue and returns false instead of throwing if the queue is full, making it the safe way to enqueue.
A queue can still be iterated without removing anything, so this loop shows the pending jobs while leaving the queue untouched.
The total is captured before processing begins, because size() shrinks with every poll and would otherwise be useless as a denominator.
Checking isEmpty before each pass is the queue-safe way to loop; it guarantees peek and poll always have something to work with.
peek returns the element at the head without removing it, so the job can be announced before it is actually consumed.
poll removes and returns the head element, advancing the queue; storing the result lets the program report which job just left.
